grade_reason: Her campaign material mentions AI (a data center moratorium, regulating AI companies, a 'Democratizing AI' heading) but nothing found addresses catastrophic risk from AI. No sponsorship of the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act was found; as a first-time candidate she held no office in which to sponsor it.
notes: Eight web searches ran (none refused); none of the name-plus-topic searches (superintelligence, extinction, AI safety, pause, China) found any result mentioning her. Campaign site checked directly: the fact sheet page (https://www.kirosforco.com/fact-sheet, undated) contains the lines 'Supporting a moratorium on AI data centers' (listed under 'What They're Attacking Melat For') and 'AI companies should be regulated, not handed blank checks' (listed under 'What a Majority of Denver Voters Believe'). These are short, undated campaign list items rather than statements with a date, and the moratorium's motivation is not stated, so they are left out of statements; they are the reason for D rather than none. The priorities page (https://www.kirosforco.com/priorities-2) has a 'DEMOCRATIZING AI' heading with no body text. The fact-sheets PDF could not be decoded. Colorado Politics Q&A of 9 July 2026 opened: no AI mentions. The search tool's own summary of the campaign site contradicted itself on whether she supports or opposes the data center moratorium; the page text read directly says 'Supporting'. Identity confirmed: Melat Kiros, Democratic socialist who beat Rep. Diana DeGette in the CO-01 primary on 30 June 2026.
